narrative:
Based on your academic profile, the model estimates a 72% chance that you would not pass the bar exam on the first attempt. This high level of predicted risk is what led to the denial of your admission.

The single strongest influence on this prediction was your undergraduate GPA. At 2.60, it falls well below the 3.23 average of accepted students, and this gap weighed heavily in the model, pushing strongly toward a failure outcome.

The next most influential factor was your family's income bracket. While students from upper-middle backgrounds make up the largest share of accepted applicants at 45.4%, this characteristic nonetheless contributed a smaller but notable push toward failure in your specific case, based on patterns in the data.

Your first-year class decile also mattered, though slightly less than the first two. Being in the 7th decile means your Year 1 grades placed you behind roughly two-thirds of your classmates, while accepted students typically sit around the 6th decile. This too moved the prediction toward failure.

Taken together, these factors produced a 72% predicted failure probability, far too high to support admission.

What can you do? Strengthen your academic record before reapplying, since your undergraduate GPA is the most critical issue—retaking courses to raise it or achieving a strong master's degree would directly address the model's main concern. For your class decile, focus on demonstrating early, consistent academic performance in any future program. And while your family income cannot be changed, you can use your application to explain any external challenges that affected your past scores. Rebuilding your profile in these key areas will give you a substantially better chance of admission next time.
